heroHeadline: Goldman Cuts US Recession Probability to 15% (June 6); ECB Hike June 11 at 99%; BOJ June 16 at 96%+; Warsh Inaugural FOMC June 16-17; 'No Landing' Now Base Case; Iran MOU Day 9 Unsigned; Section 122 Cliff 47 Days
heroSubtitle: Goldman Sachs formally revised its 12-month US recession probability to 15% — the lowest of the Warsh era — following the May 2026 nonfarm payrolls blowout (+172,000 vs. ~85,000 consensus, released June 5). The 'no landing' scenario is now Goldman's base case: the US economy is growing above trend while inflation remains above the 2% target, requiring the Warsh Fed to hold or hike rather than cut. Goldman simultaneously warned of a 'paycheck recession' where real incomes are eroding at a pace almost never seen outside official recessions — driven by tariff pass-through (CPI 3.8%) and Iran war energy prices (PPI 6.0%). The June 5 market reaction confirmed the 'good news is bad news' dynamic: S&P 500 fell 2.6% to 7,383.74 (worst day since October 2025), Nasdaq fell 4.2%, and 2-year Treasury yields hit 4.162% — the highest since February 2025 — as December 2026 rate hike probability was fully priced for the first time in the Warsh era. The most consequential macro week of the year opens Monday, June 8: the ECB meets June 11 with 99% probability of a 25bp hike to 2.25% deposit rate — the first ECB rate increase since July 2023, reversing the easing cycle triggered by the post-COVID inflation fight. The BOJ meets June 16 with 96%+ probability of a 25bp hike to 1.00% — the highest Japanese rate since 2008 — with Bloomberg (June 4) confirming BOJ officials are mulling the move. Critically, the BOJ decision releases simultaneous with Warsh's inaugural FOMC Day 1 (June 16-17), creating the August 2024 'Black Monday II' yen carry-trade unwind scenario: if BOJ hikes and Warsh signals a December hike in his first dot plot, the estimated $4 trillion in yen-funded carry trades begins unwinding — replicating the August 5, 2024 session that saw the Nikkei fall 12% and VIX spike to 65. Warsh's June 17 Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) and dot plot are the defining policy deliverables of his chairmanship so far: Does the dot show 0 cuts, 0 hikes, or 1 hike for 2026? Does he accelerate QT toward his $4-5T balance sheet target? Does he pivot from headline PCE to the trimmed-mean gauge? The Iran MOU remains unsigned on Day 9 (June 7) — Brent crude hovers ~$93-97, above Goldman's $88 recession-reset threshold. A signed deal before June 16 would ease Warsh's inflation inputs and could soften his dot plot; continued stalemate locks in a hawkish signal. JPMorgan (35%) and Moody's Analytics (49%) have not yet formally updated their recession probabilities after the NFP blowout — both are expected to revise down toward Goldman's 15-20% range. The Section 122 tariff cliff (July 24, 47 days) requires Congressional action; the Section 301 tariff probe on 60 economies (announced June 3) provides the administration's legal fallback architecture.
footerNote: Data sourced from: Goldman Sachs — 12-month US recession probability cut to 15% (June 6, 2026); Bloomberg — BOJ mulling 25bp June 16 hike to 1.00% (June 4, 2026); ECB April 30 press conference — signals June 11 'new assessment'; BLS — May 2026 Employment Situation, NFP +172K (June 5, 2026); Yahoo Finance / TheStreet — S&P 500 –2.6% to 7,383.74 (June 5, 2026); US Treasury — 10Y 4.544%, 30Y 5.007%, 2Y 4.162% (June 5 close); Fortune — Goldman 'paycheck recession' warning (June 2, 2026); Axios — Iran MOU status, Day 9 unsigned (June 7, 2026). Critical path: ECB June 11 (25bp hike 99%) → BOJ June 16 (25bp hike 96%+) → Warsh inaugural FOMC June 16-17 (dot plot) → Section 122 cliff July 24 (47 days). Goldman 15% / JPMorgan 35% / Moody's 49% (latter two pre-June 5, updates pending).
